clue.text: River given to another, backing onto a third?

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
taken as written

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the second river is read right to left

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge, another river after the first

explanation.surface: A puzzle of rivers flowing into one another, one turning back to meet a third.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns CAM into MAC. The three rivers chain PO, TO and MAC, and the result is itself a third river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac flows through Washington DC, so it is a further river, a third after the Po and the Cam.

clue.text: Reasonably fair

definitions.meaning: fairly or moderately, as in quite good

explanation.definitionFit: Pretty is an adverb meaning fairly or quite, and an adjective meaning good-looking.

clue.text: See 26
Test God as Cupid?

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
God is the Maker, the creator

explanation.surface: Putting the deity on trial in the role of the god of love.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a five-day international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid brings lovers together, so he is an example of someone who arranges matches; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Young animal, it's the measure of the Ark?

parts.note: a cub is the young of a fox, lion or bear
the 's is the verb is, a link, leaving the word it

explanation.surface: A small creature wondering whether it is the size of Noah's Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's Ark was specified in cubits, an ancient length measured from elbow to fingertip.

clue.text: Flying tooth?

parts.note: a slang word for a tooth is also slang for a helicopter, so the same word names a tooth that flies

explanation.definitionFit: Teeth are called choppers in slang, and so is a helicopter, the flying sense.

clue.text: Once an old sort of architectural feature

indicators.note: to sort letters is to arrange them, so these words are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Something that was once a kind of ancient building feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges ONCEANOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonnade is a row of columns, a classic feature of buildings.

clue.text: Beefy type crosses state to find gem

indicators.note: the ox goes across the state, so its letters lie either side

parts.note: an ox is a beef animal
NY is the abbreviation for New York state

explanation.surface: A burly man travels across a state looking for a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beefy type' sounds like a burly man, but it is the animal that gives us beef; 'crosses' means it straddles the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Worker nursing infant, cut, it's presumed

indicators.note: a worker nursing a baby holds it inside their arms, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: prole is short for proletarian, a worker

indicators.note: cut means the last letter of the word for infant is removed

parts.note: an infant is a baby

explanation.surface: A worker holding a baby, injured, is the likely assumption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' is the Marxist sense, a member of the working class; 'cut' only shortens the infant, not the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something probable is likely, so it is taken as given or assumed.

clue.text: Bird bringing itinerant Shed into line

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go into the word for line

parts.note: a rank is a line, as of soldiers

indicators.note: itinerant means wandering, so the word shed moves its letters about

explanation.surface: Bringing a wandering shed into a straight row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a garden building, but it is just four letters set wandering by 'itinerant' before going 'into' the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The redshank is a wading bird with red legs.

clue.text: Turn out as tennis player, once

definitions.meaning: to turn something inside out, as an eyelid
Chris ..., the American champion of the 1970s and 80s

explanation.definitionFit: To evert is the technical verb for turning outwards; Chris Evert won eighteen Grand Slam singles titles.

clue.text: Here, all singing, all dancing champagne club

parts.note: Bolly is the British nickname for Bollinger champagne
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A glitzy nightclub with champagne and a full song-and-dance show.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLLY is British slang for Bollinger champagne. The definition is a playful description of the place whose films are famous for song and dance numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bollywood, the Mumbai film industry, is known for musicals packed with singing and dancing.

clue.text: Standard Shakespearean character

definitions.meaning: a benchmark or criterion against which things are judged
the clown in As You Like It

explanation.definitionFit: A touchstone was a stone used to test gold, hence any benchmark; it is also the jester's name in As You Like It.

clue.text: See 27
Choose bulk to reconstruct reinforced building

indicators.note: reconstructing rebuilds something in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Selecting bulk materials to rebuild a fortified structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reconstruct' rearranges CHOOSEBULK.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockhouse is a fortified military structure, typically of concrete.

clue.text: Idea for reconstruction ruins everything in never-never land, almost entirely

parts.note: to ruin something is to mar it, so ruins gives mars

indicators.note: in places the word for everything inside the never-never letters

parts.note: the never-never is British slang for hire purchase, abbreviated HP
everything means all

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped from the word land

explanation.surface: A scheme to rebuild that spoils everything in a fantasy land.
explanation.walkthrough: The never-never is British slang for buying on hire purchase; 'in' places everything within it, and 'almost entirely' leaves land one letter short.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marshall Plan was the American programme to rebuild Western Europe after the Second World War.

clue.text: Strong leader brutal, in possession of strong muscles, say

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the word for brutal holds the strong letter inside it

parts.note: hellish means dreadful or brutal
F is forte, the musical abbreviation for loud or strong

explanation.surface: A powerful, harsh leader with a muscular physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in possession of' puts F inside HELLISH. The definition plays on muscles sounding like mussels, which are shellfish; 'say' marks both the example and the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Mussels, which sound like muscles, are an example of molluscs eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Bold fashion seen through swirling mist

indicators.note: the fashion word is seen through the mist, lying within it
swirling mist moves around, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: mode means fashion or style

explanation.surface: A daring style glimpsed through swirling fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bold' is the definition in the sense of brazen, not brave; 'swirling' stirs the mist and 'seen through' sets the fashion word within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodest means forward or shameless, a sense of bold.

clue.text: Variable indefinite number triples, which proves an irritation

indicators.note: variable means changeable, so these letters change their order

parts.note: n stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A maths note about changing numbers tripling that turns out to be annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variable' rearranges N and TRIPLES. N is the maths symbol for any number.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter is a sliver lodged in the skin, a nagging irritation.

clue.text: Site coordinates parental choice?

parts.note: ma is a parent, standing for the parental part
a preference is a choice

explanation.surface: A mother gets her pick of where things go.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as 'Ma's preference', a parental choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A map reference is a set of grid coordinates locating a site on a map.

clue.text: Pulse tester has to fix Penelope's heart

parts.note: to mend is to fix

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A doctor checking someone's pulse must cure Penelope's heart condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the middle letters of Penelope, EL. 'Pulse tester' looks medical, but pulses are peas and beans.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregor Mendel founded genetics through breeding experiments on peas, which are pulses.

clue.text: Imagine fish shop

parts.note: I bet means I imagine or suppose
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Picture a fish shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' is the British slang verb for informing on someone, not a store.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone, in British slang, is to inform on them, which is to betray them.

clue.text: Poet writing about primo donno?

indicators.note: writing the word about face, backwards, is the reversal signal here

parts.note: a jokey male form of prima donna, a divo

explanation.surface: A poet composing a piece about a male opera star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writing about' turns DIVO, a male diva, backwards. 'Primo donno' is a mock-masculine form of prima donna.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman poet of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Vulgar VIP's veiny victuals

parts.note: blue means smutty or vulgar, as in blue jokes
a big cheese is a VIP

explanation.surface: A crude celebrity's unappetising food.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of VIP's is only a link to what follows; a VIP is a big cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue cheese such as Stilton is marbled with mould veins, so it is veined food.

clue.text: Two names among union of nations, one showing tiredness

indicators.note: the two names sit among the letters for the union

parts.note: EU is the European Union
N is the abbreviation for name, so two names is NN
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Two people in a union of countries, one of them looking weary.
explanation.walkthrough: N for name is a standard abbreviation; 'among' sets the two of them within the European grouping, with 'one' added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a weariness of spirit.

clue.text: Opponent wanting to play a part

indicators.note: the answer plays a part within the next word, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: An adversary eager to take a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to play a part' points at letters lying inside 'wanting'.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is someone against something, an opponent.

clue.text: So relaxation now — or something more?

definitions.text: So relaxation now — or something more?

parts.words: So relaxation now — or something more?
parts.note: relaxing means stress is a thing of the past, split as former stress; or read as a word for an addition

explanation.definitionFit: An extension is an addition that makes something more; split, the word reads as former stress, which describes relaxation.

clue.text: Possible beach bums lying so?

definitions.meaning: in the phrase everything imaginable, anything existing anywhere at all

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means anywhere in existence, hence anything conceivable; sunbathers lie literally beneath the sun.

clue.text: Kit? It's not required: Ah! Bits hurt when massaged — here?

indicators.note: massaging works things over, so these letters are kneaded into a new order
something not required is dropped, so the word it goes from kit

parts.note: the 's is not a letter; it gives the word it

explanation.surface: No kit needed, and it hurts when bits are massaged: a sauna-style session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not required' takes IT from KIT, leaving K; 'when massaged' rearranges K with AHBITSHURT. Kit is British for clothes, so no kit means naked, which fits the steam room.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the place it means: a steam bath where people strip off and are massaged.

clue.text: I don't hurry squeezing sweetheart in a perfect world

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: squeezing holds the sweetheart letter tight inside the word for not hurrying

parts.note: to dally is to dawdle rather than hurry
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Someone saying they take their time hugging their beloved in an ideal world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeezing' puts E inside DALLY to make DEALLY. Sweetheart is read as the heart of sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means in the best of circumstances, the way things would be if all were perfect.
